원자료 R09843의 적용 맥락: This paper studies long-run economic effects of Catholic patron saint day festival timing across Mexican municipalities, focusing on the historical New Spain region. It combines officially-prescribed saint-day dates (set since Spanish colonial conquest) with FAO-GAEZ estimates of local maize planting and harvest cycles to analyze municipality-level outcomes (primarily 2010 census and agricultural data). The authors evaluate whether festivals coinciding with planting or harvest reduce agricultural productivity, hinder structural transformation, and affect income, religiosity, and social capital.
